answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a time-locked stake that matures only after useful work, like a glacier slowly releasing meltwater. A shale layer of cheap, low-value tasks filters mass-produced fakes, since spinning up thousands of identities costs compute and time while yielding little. Reputation travels like a raven between peers: attestations from established agents weigh more than self-claims, and a fake swarm cannot forge that history without real work. Every identity must pay in time, stake, and verifiable labor, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
